t.1.195.1: Bhīṣma said: A quarrel with the sons of Pāṇḍu does not please me in any way. Just as Dhṛtarāṣṭra is to me, so too, without doubt, is Pāṇḍu.
t.1.195.2: Just as the sons of Gāndhārī are regarded, so are the sons of Kuntī regarded; and just as they are to be protected by me, O Dhṛtarāṣṭra, so are they to be protected by you.
t.1.195.3: Just as they belong to me and to the king, so too do they belong to Duryodhana, and likewise to all the Kurus and to others as well, O Bhārata.
t.1.195.5: Duryodhana, my son, just as you look upon this kingdom as "my ancestral inheritance," so too do the Pāṇḍavas look upon it.
t.1.195.4: Matters having come to this, I do not favor war with them; make peace with those heroes and let the land be given to them today. This kingdom belongs to them as well, as it belonged to their great-grandfathers, the best of the Kurus, and to their father.
t.1.195.6: If those hapless Pāṇḍaveyas have not obtained the kingdom, then how indeed could this be yours either, or belong to any Bhārata at all?
t.1.195.8: Let half of the kingdom be given to them with sweetness alone, for this, O tiger among men, is beneficial for all the people as well.
t.1.195.7: Now, bull of the Bharatas, if you have obtained the kingdom by dharma, then they too obtained the kingdom, and even before you. Such is my view.
t.1.195.9: If it is done otherwise than this, it will not be for our good; and for you too there will be complete disgrace, there is no doubt.
t.1.195.10: Devote yourself to guarding your fame, for fame is the highest strength. The life of a man whose fame is lost is held to be fruitless.
t.1.195.11: As long as a man's fame does not perish, O Kaurava, so long does he live, O Gāndhāri; but he whose fame is lost is himself lost.
t.1.195.12: Take up this very dharma, befitting the lineage of the Kurus; O mighty-armed one, make yourselves worthy of your forebears.
t.1.195.13: By good fortune those heroes survive, by good fortune Pṛthā lives, and by good fortune the wicked Purocana has gone to his end with his desire unfulfilled.
t.1.195.14: From that time on, O son of Gāndhārī, ever since I heard that Kuntī had met such a fate, I have not been able to look upon any living being in the world.
t.1.195.17: And while those heroes live, O joy of the Kurus, their ancestral share cannot be taken away, not even by the wielder of the thunderbolt himself.
t.1.195.15: Nor indeed do people hold Purocana to blame for that wrong so much as they hold you to blame, O tiger among men.
t.1.195.18: For they all stand firm in dharma, and all are of one mind; and they have been unjustly driven out, especially from a kingdom to which they have an equal claim.
t.1.195.16: Therefore, great king, this survival of theirs, which wipes away your guilt, should be welcomed, and so should the sight of the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.195.19: If righteousness is to be done by you, if what is dear to me is to be done, and if their welfare is to be secured, let half be given to them.
